item.title: Version 1.6.58
item.description: When the alt-codec download succeeds, both files now share one combined archive-info.txt (same show, same source) instead of two near-duplicate documents.

item.title: Version 1.6.57
item.description: Every download now gets an auto-generated archive-info.txt (title, channel, URL, measured codec/bitrate/file size, format IDs) alongside the usual sidecar files. Also drops the date prefix from generated filenames.

item.title: Version 1.6.56
item.description: Optional per-video toggle: if YouTube offers Premium in two different video codecs for a video, downloads both as separate files (primary + ALT), each with their own full set of sidecar files.

item.title: Version 1.6.55
item.description: The .ytdlp.log sidecar now puts the DOWNLOADED summary first instead of last, and bolds the actually-downloaded row(s) in the available-formats table.

item.title: Version 1.6.54
item.description: Parallel downloads (two premieres no longer block each other), a confirmed-best-quality badge visible right in the Tracked list, Dutch+English subtitles, and a fix for a false 'still not live' notification on already-published videos.

item.title: Version 1.6.53
item.description: The .ytdlp.log now starts with the complete list of every quality YouTube offers for that video (same info as "yt-dlp -F") and ends with exactly which one got downloaded — so you can verify it really was the best available without running anything manually.

item.title: Version 1.6.52
item.description: Fixed: the subtitle download could accidentally grab YouTube's live-chat replay instead of real subtitles on a video with no English subtitles but an archived live chat — found while downloading a real video. Excluded specifically, real subtitle behavior unchanged.

item.title: Version 1.6.51
item.description: Every VOD now confirms whether it really got the best possible quality for that exact video — not just a label, but an explicit check against what was actually available, shown as ✅ confirmed best available or ⚠️ lower than expected in the push notification and log.

item.title: Version 1.6.50
item.description: Official subtitles (not auto-generated captions) are now saved as .srt alongside the video, thumbnail, description, and log — same name, same folder.

item.title: Version 1.6.49
item.description: Bug fixes from a review of this week's changes: a label with a "/" (e.g. an artist name like AC/DC) could silently break the failure log; a video titled with "[LIVE]" in it could get the quality label spliced in twice; Add could be clicked before a lookup finished; editing an old Premium-quality premiere after turning Premium off could show no quality selected; a single unattended network hiccup could disable cookies for up to a day.

item.title: Version 1.6.48
item.description: Every download (LIVE and VOD) now saves a complete, unfiltered yt-dlp log next to the video — the full transcript from the first fragment to the end, not just the curated progress lines already shown in the app itself.

item.title: Version 1.6.47
item.description: Every download now also saves the real YouTube thumbnail (full resolution, as .jpg) and, when available, a text file with the video's description and chapters — all three files share the same name as the video.

item.title: Version 1.6.46
item.description: New "I have YouTube Premium" toggle in Settings > Quality — turns on 1080p Premium directly, instead of needing to Look Up a specific video known to have it first before the option ever appears on a fresh install.

item.title: Version 1.6.45
item.description: Quality tab in Settings now matches the look of the rest of Settings — the picker sizes to its content instead of sitting at an arbitrary fixed width, and the explanation text uses the same font size and spacing as every other tab.

item.title: Version 1.6.44
item.description: Fixed messy button layout on Upcoming rows — Dismiss and Add are now matched, properly centered buttons instead of mismatched text-vs-button floating above the row.

item.title: Version 1.6.43
item.description: Trimmed the new Quality settings tab — the explanation text was way too long for the window. Same information, much shorter.

item.title: Version 1.6.42
item.description: New Quality tab in Settings: set a default quality for new premieres, plus a plain-language explanation of what 1080p Premium means and why the Add screen's quality list is sometimes the full generic one instead of only what's actually available (only possible once a video is a finished VOD).

item.title: Version 1.6.41
item.description: The quality dropdown now shows only the resolutions (and Premium) that genuinely exist for that specific video when Look Up can check — same as YouTube's own quality menu. A premiere looked up before it airs (no format list yet) still falls back to the general list, resolved for real at download time.

item.title: Version 1.6.40
item.description: Reprise now checks once a day whether YouTube actually accepts your login cookies (the same check as "Test YouTube login" in Settings), automatically — not just when you manually click that button. A rejected login now shows up as a clear warning right away.

item.title: Version 1.6.39
item.description: Clicking Add on an Upcoming (discovered) premiere no longer tracks it instantly — it now opens the same Add dialog, pre-filled with the title and URL, with the scheduled time filled in automatically, so you can pick a download quality before it's actually added.

item.title: Version 1.6.38
item.description: Fixed: "Log in to YouTube again" (Settings > Cookies) always opened Chrome, even with Safari explicitly selected as the cookie source — so logging in there didn't actually help. Now opens whichever browser is actually configured.

item.title: Version 1.6.37
item.description: Fixed a bug that could silently cut download quality to 360p: a custom sort setting combined with a loosely-scoped format selector sometimes let the low-quality single-stream fallback outrank the real 1080p/720p track, independent of the quality you picked. Verified fixed end-to-end.

item.title: Version 1.6.36
item.description: New channel-discovery bug fix (scheduled premieres were sometimes missed because the app only checked a channel's /streams tab, which YouTube hides for merely-scheduled content). New: choose download quality per premiere (Best available, 1080p/720p/480p/360p, or YouTube Premium's enhanced bitrate if your account has it — matches YouTube's own quality menu). The chosen quality now also shows up in the VOD-complete notification.

item.title: Version 1.6.32
item.description: No functional changes — just a version bump so you can personally test the Sparkle update flow end to end.

item.title: Version 1.6.31
item.description: Fixed a bug where Sparkle's own update dialog could get silently closed if you reopened the main Reprise window while an update was sitting at Ready to Install — discarding an already-downloaded update with no warning. Also: the Upcoming tab label no longer wraps onto two lines when its notification badge appears.

item.title: Version 1.6.26
item.description: Small fix: the Upcoming tab label could wrap onto two lines when its notification badge appeared.

item.title: Version 1.6.25
item.description: Reprise now checks for updates automatically (via Sparkle) instead of needing a manual check in Settings. A dialog appears on its own when a new version is out, with release notes and Skip/Remind Later/Install choices.
